newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar says Bahrain tortured Qatari spy suspect.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says Bahrain tortured Qatari spy suspect.

text.p: Qatar said on Friday that Bahrain had tortured a Qatari man to obtain a confession of spying for Doha, setting what it called a dangerous precedent in Gulf Arab ties.
An interior ministry statement also placed the responsibility of the safety of the man and a Qatari woman, who are standing trial in Bahrain on spying charges on Manama.
The two appeared in court on Wednesday in Bahrain, which is locked in a bitter territorial dispute with Qatar. The case was postponed until December 14.
If found guilty they could be executed or face long prison sentences, lawyers said.

The Qatari statement on Friday said that Hamad al-Baker had informed the ministry after attending the trial in Bahrain that his son, Fahd, was "exposed to various methods of torture which was clearly evident on his body".

Qatar again denied that the two suspects, Fahad Hamad Abdullah al-Baker and Salwa Jassim Mohammed Fakhri, were spying for it and a Qatari official later told Reuters that Fahd had denied the charge in court but had signed a confession under torture.
"His arrest sets a dangerous precedent in Gulf ties," the statement said. "Any verdicts against the two would be considered void as they are passed under duress in violation of international norms."
The Qatari official said: "The timing of the case is illogical." This was a reference to the annual Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) which opens in Doha on Saturday.

Bahrain has said it would not attend the summit because of unfriendly policies. The other GCC members, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Oman, Qatar and Kuwait, have all said they would participate.
